evidence: This is a factual statement about the mouse Cre/lox resource, supported by citation.

claim: The lack of embryonic stem cell technology and inefficient homologous recombination in the early embryo necessitated alternative approaches to generate Cre/lox tools in zebrafish.
source: In zebrafish, the lack of embryonic stem cell technology and inefficient homologous recombination in the early embryo necessitated alternative approaches to generate Cre/lox tools (Carney and Mosimann, 2018).
evidence: This explains the technical challenges in zebrafish that motivated alternative approaches, supported by citation.

claim: Tol2 transposon transgenesis combined with defined promoters or BAC recombineering has been used to develop Cre lines in zebrafish.
source: Tol2 transposon transgenesis (Balciunas et al., 2006; Kawakami et al., 2000) combined with defined promoters (Mosimann et al., 2011) or BAC recombineering (Förster et al., 2017) has been used to develop Cre lines, and a rich source of zebrafish cell-type-specific Cre drivers has been generated by random Tol2 transposon enhancer trap screens (Jungke et al., 2015; Marquart et al., 2015; Tabor et al., 2019; Zhong et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes established methods for generating Cre drivers in zebrafish, supported by multiple citations.

claim: A rich source of zebrafish cell-type-specific Cre drivers has been generated by random Tol2 transposon enhancer trap screens.
source: Tol2 transposon transgenesis (Balciunas et al., 2006; Kawakami et al., 2000) combined with defined promoters (Mosimann et al., 2011) or BAC recombineering (Förster et al., 2017) has been used to develop Cre lines, and a rich source of zebrafish cell-type-specific Cre drivers has been generated by random Tol2 transposon enhancer trap screens (Jungke et al., 2015; Marquart et al., 2015; Tabor et al., 2019; Zhong et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the outcome of enhancer trap screens for generating Cre drivers, supported by citations.

claim: Cre/lox regulated conditional control of gene function in zebrafish was previously limited to generation of knock out alleles by random Tol2 transposon insertional mutagenesis with a floxed/FRT gene trap.
source: Cre/lox regulated conditional control of gene function in zebrafish was previously limited to generation of knock out alleles by random Tol2 transposon insertional mutagenesis with a floxed/FRT gene trap, which can be reverted by Cre or Flip-mediated recombination (Clark et al., 2011; Ni et al., 2012; Trinh et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the historical limitation of conditional genetics in zebrafish, supported by citations.

claim: Gene editing methods have been developed in zebrafish to simplify Cre driver isolation and generate genuine lox-regulated conditional alleles by targeted integration.
source: Only recently have gene editing methods been developed in zebrafish to simplify Cre driver isolation (Almeida et al., 2021; Kesavan et al., 2018) and generate genuine lox-regulated conditional alleles by targeted integration (Burg et al., 2018; Han et al., 2021; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Li et al., 2019; Sugimoto et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes recent advances in zebrafish conditional genetics, supported by multiple citations.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 targeted integration is an efficient method to isolate zebrafish proneural specific Cre and CreERT2 drivers that are expressed under the control of endogenous gene regulatory elements.
source: We and others recently demonstrated CRISPR-Cas9 targeted integration is an efficient method to isolate zebrafish proneural specific Cre and CreERT2 drivers that are expressed under the control of endogenous gene regulatory elements (Almeida et al., 2021; Kesavan et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes a method demonstrated by the authors and others, supported by citations.

claim: TALENs were first used to introduce loxP sequences directly into the zebrafish genome by somatic gene targeting.
source: Efforts to introduce loxP sequences directly into the zebrafish genome by somatic gene targeting was first described using TALENs to target a double-strand break in the cdrh2 gene, followed by repair from a DNA oligonucleotide template containing homologous sequences flanking a loxP site (Bedell et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the first demonstration of direct loxP site insertion in zebrafish, supported by citation.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 was used to create a floxed allele in two zebrafish genes by sequential loxP oligonucleotide targeting at sites flanking an exon.
source: This approach was expanded upon using CRISPR-Cas9 to create a floxed allele in two zebrafish genes by sequential loxP oligonucleotide targeting at sites flanking an exon, and demonstrated robust gene knockdown and loss of function after Cre-mediated exon excision (Burg et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes an expansion of the loxP insertion approach using CRISPR-Cas9, supported by citation.

claim: A single integration event of a floxed cassette with a linked reporter has distinct advantages over sequential loxP insertions, including only one generation of targeting and fluorescent genotyping of the integration allele.
source: Although this approach is effective for creating a Cre/lox regulated allele, a single integration event of a floxed cassette with a linked reporter has distinct advantages, including only one generation of targeting and fluorescent genotyping of the integration allele.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the advantages of single integration events.

claim: The first example of a germline floxed conditional allele with linked reporter used a single TALEN site downstream of an exon.
source: The first example of a germline floxed conditional allele with linked reporter used a single TALEN site downstream of an exon (Hoshijima et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the first demonstration of a specific approach, supported by citation.

claim: A zebrafish conditional shha allele was isolated by integration of a modified Flex invertible gene trap called Zwitch by homologous recombination from an intact plasmid.
source: A similar strategy using long homology arms was used to isolate a zebrafish conditional shha allele by integration of a modified Flex invertible gene trap (Ni et al., 2012), called Zwitch, by homologous recombination from an intact plasmid (Sugimoto et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes a specific conditional allele generation strategy, supported by citations.

claim: Stable inversion of the Zwitch cassette by Cre led to effective shha gene knockdown and defective shha signaling.
source: Stable inversion of the Zwitch cassette by Cre led to effective shha gene knockdown and defective shha signaling.
evidence: This describes the functional outcome of the Zwitch system, based on cited work.

claim: Homology-independent targeting strategies have been described to generate conditional knockouts with a linked reporter, or bidirectional knockin of a dual reporter gene trap cassette.
source: More recently homology-independent targeting strategies have been described to generate conditional knockouts with a linked reporter, or bidirectional knockin of a dual reporter gene trap cassette, providing a method for labeling conditional gene knockout cells (Han et al., 2021; Li et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes recent alternative approaches to conditional allele generation, supported by citations.

claim: Rapid tissue-specific gene knockdown and cell labeling can be achieved by somatic targeting with a floxed Cas9-2A-GFP; U6:gRNA transposon in a Cre-specific transgenic background.
source: As an alternative to isolation of stable germline conditional alleles, rapid tissue-specific gene knockdown and cell labeling can be achieved by somatic targeting with a floxed Cas9-2A-GFP; U6:gRNA transposon in a Cre-specific transgenic background, allowing for simultaneous bi-allelic inactivation with GFP cell labeling (Hans et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes an alternative somatic approach to conditional gene knockdown, supported by citation.

claim: There is still a need for a simple method to efficiently recover robust conditional alleles through a single gene engineering event.
source: Together, these approaches provide effective conditional gene knockdown strategies with varying degrees of complexity in design and execution. However, there is still a need for a simple method to efficiently recover robust conditional alleles through a single gene engineering event.
evidence: This is a statement identifying a remaining gap in the field despite existing methods.

claim: The GeneWeld strategy simplifies targeting vector assembly and enhances the efficiency of on target integration.
source: We previously showed our GeneWeld strategy simplifies targeting vector assembly and enhances the efficiency of on target integration (Almeida et al., 2021; Wierson et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the advantages of the GeneWeld strategy demonstrated in previous work, supported by citations.

claim: The UFlip vector is derived from the GeneWeld pGTag and pPRISM targeted integration vectors and the Tol2 Gene Breaking Transposon vectors.
source: In the present study, we built a universal vector, UFlip, which is derived from the GeneWeld pGTag and pPRISM targeted integration vectors (Almeida et al., 2021; Wierson et al., 2020), and the Tol2 Gene Breaking Transposon vectors (Clark et al., 2011; Ichino et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the origin and design of the UFlip vector, supported by citations.

claim: The UFlip cassette contains a 2A-mRFP primary reporter based on the Tol2 RP2 gene trap.
source: In the UFlip vector, homology arm cloning sites flank a floxed gene trap cassette that contains a 2A-mRFP primary reporter based on the Tol2 RP2 gene trap (Clark et al., 2011; Ichino et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes a component of the UFlip design, supported by citations.

claim: The UFlip cassette contains a heart or lens BFP secondary reporter for transgenic identification.
source: The cassette also contains a heart or lens BFP secondary reporter for transgenic identification.
evidence: This describes another component of the UFlip design.

claim: Integration alleles with UFlip in the active, gene 'off' orientation show mRFP expression from the gene trap in the expected gene-specific pattern.
source: Integration alleles with UFlip in the active, gene 'off' orientation show mRFP expression from the gene trap in the expected gene-specific pattern.
evidence: This describes the reporter expression pattern observed in 'off' alleles.

claim: UFlip 'off' alleles lead to >99% knock down of gene expression compared to wild-type levels.
source: UFlip 'off' alleles lead to >99% knock down of gene expression compared to wild-type levels and recapitulate indel mutant phenotypes, demonstrating highly effective loss of function by primary transcript splicing into the gene trap.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement of gene knockdown efficiency.

claim: UFlip 'off' alleles recapitulate indel mutant phenotypes, demonstrating highly effective loss of function by primary transcript splicing into the gene trap.
source: UFlip 'off' alleles lead to >99% knock down of gene expression compared to wild-type levels and recapitulate indel mutant phenotypes, demonstrating highly effective loss of function by primary transcript splicing into the gene trap.
evidence: This describes the phenotypic validation of the 'off' alleles and infers the mechanism.

source: Recombination of an 'off' allele by Cre injection or a transgenic Cre source leads loss of RFP expression, stable inversion of the UFlip cassette to the passive orientation, and robust conditional rescue of mutant phenotypes.
evidence: This describes the reporter expression outcome after Cre-mediated recombination.

claim: Recombination of an 'off' allele by Cre injection or a transgenic Cre source leads to stable inversion of the UFlip cassette to the passive orientation.
source: Recombination of an 'off' allele by Cre injection or a transgenic Cre source leads loss of RFP expression, stable inversion of the UFlip cassette to the passive orientation, and robust conditional rescue of mutant phenotypes.
evidence: This describes the molecular outcome of Cre-mediated recombination.

claim: Recombination of an 'off' allele by Cre injection or a transgenic Cre source leads to robust conditional rescue of mutant phenotypes.
source: Recombination of an 'off' allele by Cre injection or a transgenic Cre source leads loss of RFP expression, stable inversion of the UFlip cassette to the passive orientation, and robust conditional rescue of mutant phenotypes.
evidence: This describes the functional outcome of conditional rescue.

claim: UFlip 'on' alleles are phenotypically normal in combination with loss-of-function mutations.
source: UFlip 'on' alleles are phenotypically normal in combination with loss-of-function mutations.
evidence: This demonstrates that 'on' alleles do not disrupt gene function.

claim: Recombination of an 'on' allele by Cre injection or a transgenic Cre source leads to induction of RFP expression.
source: Recombination of an 'on' allele by Cre injection or a transgenic Cre source leads to induction of RFP expression, stable cassette inversion, and robust conditional inactivation.
evidence: This describes the reporter expression outcome after conditional inactivation.

claim: Recombination of an 'on' allele by Cre injection or a transgenic Cre source leads to stable cassette inversion.
source: Recombination of an 'on' allele by Cre injection or a transgenic Cre source leads to induction of RFP expression, stable cassette inversion, and robust conditional inactivation.
evidence: This describes the molecular outcome of Cre-mediated recombination.

claim: Recombination of an 'on' allele by Cre injection or a transgenic Cre source leads to robust conditional inactivation.
source: Recombination of an 'on' allele by Cre injection or a transgenic Cre source leads to induction of RFP expression, stable cassette inversion, and robust conditional inactivation.

source: Alternating pairs of loxP and lox2272 sites oriented head to head flanking the cassette are designed to drive two Cre recombination events that invert and lock the cassette in place, a design strategy described previously to generate floxed conditional alleles in mice (Robles-Oteiza et al., 2015; Schnütgen et al., 2003) and zebrafish (Sugimoto et al., 2017).

claim: Integration of UFlip into an intron in the active, gene 'off' orientation is expected to lead to premature transcriptional termination of the primary transcript in the gene trap and splicing of upstream exons into 2A-mRFP.
source: Integration of UFlip into an intron in the active, gene 'off' orientation is expected to lead to premature transcriptional termination of the primary transcript in the gene trap and splicing of upstream exons into 2A-mRFP (Figure 1B), resulting in a loss-of-function allele.
evidence: This describes the predicted mechanism of gene inactivation by the 'off' orientation, illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Integration of UFlip into an intron in the active, gene 'off' orientation results in a loss-of-function allele.
source: Integration of UFlip into an intron in the active, gene 'off' orientation is expected to lead to premature transcriptional termination of the primary transcript in the gene trap and splicing of upstream exons into 2A-mRFP (Figure 1B), resulting in a loss-of-function allele.
evidence: This is a predicted outcome based on the design, illustrated in Figure 1B.

source: In contrast, integration of UFlip into an intron in the passive, gene 'on' orientation is not predicted to interrupt endogenous gene expression, since RNA polymerase will read through the cassette in the intron, which is then spliced out of the mature transcript (Figure 1C).
